title: Evaluating the Effect of Activity-Based Method of Teaching Mathematics on Nigerian Secondary School Students’ Achievement in Mathematics
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether an activity-based method of teaching mathematics improves secondary school students’ achievement compared with the traditional lecture method. The study is motivated by persistent poor mathematics performance among Nigerian secondary school students and the need for more effective instructional approaches.

The intervention studied was an activity-based teaching method, described as student-centered and involving hands-on activities, discussion, reading, writing, analysis, and evaluation, contrasted with lecture-based instruction. The author focused on two Senior Secondary II mathematics topics: circle geometry and construction. Achievement was measured with a researcher-developed 20-item essay mathematics test administered as both pretest and posttest.

The study was conducted with 96 Senior Secondary II students from two government-owned schools in Calabar Metropolis, Cross River State, Nigeria. Using intact classes in a pretest-posttest comparison, students were assigned to either an experimental group receiving activity-based instruction or a control group receiving lecture method instruction. After controlling for pretest scores, the activity-based group significantly outperformed the lecture group. The paper concludes that activity-based learning can improve mathematics achievement and recommends training teachers to use activity-based methods more broadly.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study with intact classes, not a randomized controlled trial. It provides direct empirical evidence but has moderate risk of bias and limited generalizability beyond the sampled schools.
impact_tier_rationale: The study shows a modest-to-medium positive effect on mathematics achievement (η2=0.261) in a secondary-school sample, which is relevant to the target population. However, the intervention is pedagogical rather than AI-based, and the evidence comes from a single small study.

finding.finding_summary: Students taught with the activity-based method outperformed those taught with the lecture method on a researcher-developed 20-item Mathematics Test covering circle geometry and construction. In the ANCOVA, the teaching-method effect was significant after controlling for pretest scores (F=114.461, p<0.001), with partial eta squared η2=0.261; the experimental group’s mean increased from 27.19 (SD=9.56) to 51.71 (SD=8.84), compared with 27.39 (SD=9.73) to 29.56 (SD=6.22) in the control group (n=96).
finding.measure: 20-item Essay Mathematics Test (pretest and posttest) on circle geometry and construction
finding.std_deviation: Experimental posttest SD=8.84; Control posttest SD=6.22
